themes: Every messenger called to worship Allah
summary_for_children: Ash-Shu'ara tells of Musa and Pharaoh, Ibrahim and his people, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. Each called people to worship Allah, and each story ends by reminding us that Allah is Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
environment_concept: Seven shores: towering walls of water either side of a path (26:63), a meadow of many noble kinds (26:7), rock-cut homes, empty (26:149) and a thicket by a market with scales (26:176-183).
architecture_and_scenery: A Nile palace terrace, a parted sea, Ibrahim's town of idols, an ark yard, the high towers of 'Ad, rock-cut homes of Thamud, Lut's town and the thicket of Madyan, linked by a coastal road.

palette.lighting: Changing light at each shore: palace gold, sea blue, rock red, thicket green
palette.atmosphere: Wind on the coast, waves, and quiet between each settlement

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A rock amphitheatre with seven standing stones in a half ring, a chime in the middle and tracks for the stones

primary_mechanic.text: Seven stones, one per chapter of the surah, each with a light beating at its own pace. Strike the chime: a ring goes out and an echo comes back from each stone, later from farther stones. Slide each stone until its echo returns on its beat; then its chapter and the refrain are read.

unique_world.narrative_structure: The sign, then tuning the seven stones (one strike can tune several)
world_assets: seven standing stones with beat lights
environment_behaviour: a ring of sound spreads from the chime and bright echoes travel back from each stone
tuned stones turn pale and their lights stay on
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn the seven stories of Ash-Shu'ara and their shared refrain, and that a farther wall sends an echo back later

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Messengers' Stories
story_library.children_narration: Musa was sent to confront Pharaoh. Ibrahim invited his people to think about what they worshipped. Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, and Shu'ayb each warned their communities and invited them toward guidance. These stories remind us that truthfulness and sincerity matter more than wealth or status.

world_idea.title: Seven Ancient Worlds
world_idea.description: Travel through distinct narrative chapters, including an Egyptian setting, a rock-carved settlement, and a marketplace where children learn about honest measurement.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: This surah's chapters overlap with A'raf (7), Hud (11) and Al-Qamar (54). It gets its own echo mechanic so the worlds stay different.
